newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares end mixed, Thai frenzy lifts OTCs.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares end mixed, Thai frenzy lifts OTCs.

text.p: Singapore shares ended mixed as punters rushed into Malaysian over-the-counter and small issues fuelled by the feverish Thai stock market, dealers said.
Retail buyers were hopeful the rise would trigger spillover demand for Malaysian counters.

Dealers said the rise was stimulated by Thailand's central bank, which announced earlier on Wednesday that its currency would be governed by a managed flotation and would no longer be set against a basket of currencies dominated by the U.S. dollar.

"The Thai market rally is sucking in foreigners. If they sniff there, the thinking is that they will sniff further south," a dealer with a local brokerage said, noting that small local stocks were also in favour.
The UOB OTC index of Malaysian over-the-counter stocks rose 11.54 points to 1,146.18.
Meanwhile, the benchmark Straits Times Industrials Index (STII) was down 12.37 points at 1,968.91.
Dealers said institutions were mostly cautious but indulged in some selective buying of blue chips.
After its slide on Wednesday, some dealers said they thought a mild recovery was on the cards for Thursday.
Foreign tranches of banks and Singapore Airlines drew good demand with volumes expected to pick up on better participation from funds.
UOB foreign rose Singapore 40 cents to S$$15.30, DBS foreign rose 30 cents to S$$18.70, and OCBC foreign was up 10 cents at S$14.90.
New-listings stayed in lead position on turnover.
Raffles Medical Group rose 12 cents to S$1.04, while Tye Soon was up 1.5 cents to S$0.52.
